question.prompt:
Jerry cuts a wedge from a \(6\)-cm cylinder of bologna as shown by the dashed curve. Which answer choice is closest to the volume of his wedge in cubic centimeters?

[Figure 1](figures/2008_AMC_8_Q21_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
The useful observation is that the slanted cut divides the cylinder into two matching wedges. The cut runs from the bottom of one circular end to the top of the other. Turning the cylinder end for end while exchanging top and bottom swaps the two pieces, so they have equal volumes. The wedge therefore has half the cylinder's volume.

The figure gives a diameter of \(8\) cm and a cylinder length of \(6\) cm. Thus the radius is \(8\div2=4\) cm. Cylinder volume equals circular base area times length, so the wedge has volume
\[
V=\frac12\cdot\pi\cdot4^2\cdot6
=48\pi\text{ cm}^3.
\]
Using \(\pi\approx3.14\), we obtain \(V\approx150.72\text{ cm}^3\). The closest listed value is \(\boxed{151\text{ cm}^3}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
solutions.title: Use symmetry and cylinder volume
